newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan eyes 30,000 tonnes sugar for April delivery.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan eyes 30,000 tonnes sugar for April delivery.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp plans to tender privately in New York soon for a 30,000-tonne shipment of sugar to fulfil its current fiscal buying plan, a company official said on Wednesday.
The tender will be by invitation only in New York City, specifying shipment for April delivery, the official said.
The state company is on track to import 120,000 tonnes of sugar in fiscal year 1996/97, which began last July 1, she said.

Taiwan Sugar has bought 90,000 tonnes of sugar in the fiscal year to date, including 60,000 tonnes arranged through a three-year term supply deal negotiated privately with British specialist supplier Czarnikow Sugar, she said.
The 60,000 tonnes per year Czarnikow pact still leaves Taiwan Sugar 30,000 tonnes short of meeting its 120,000 tonne fiscal purchasing plan.
Taiwan Sugar, like most state companies on the rapidly liberalising island, is under mandate to privatise. But the cabinet ruled on June 27 that it would not face serious competition before 2002.
